One cell = one 3.5 m battle square.
The small number in a cell = its level (1 level = 1.75 m).
0 = sand at the sea. 1 = the stone quay, 1.75 m up.
a timber pier over the water
the main way (the Mountain Road), 3 squares
a walk-in building; orange = its door
a ledge: you fall the way of the arrow
THE BUILDINGS (inside = the same squares as outside)
one room: the harbour master’s desk, ledgers, a strongbox, a
an open-fronted hall: fish tables, baskets, boxes of ice and
a tall shed open to the slip: a hull on the stocks, timber,
two floors: nets and sails below, a sleeping loft above
a thick-walled store house: rice bales, barrels, a ladder to the
two floors: a common room with low tables and a hearth, a
one room: bunks, a hearth, hung fish
a stone harbour light: a stair inside, the fire room on top (the
The main way leaves the pier, crosses the open square, turns
twice and climbs the Harbour Gate stair into the City.
Two ledges drop into the bay from the City above (6 to 1
behind the market, 3 to 1 into the rice store’s yard).
The head: a thin trail climbs it in right-angle legs to the
lantern tower; a ledge drops you to the small beach.
Level on purpose: the square, both quays, the beach.
Faded plots at the top belong to the City, not to this sample.
KATANA BAY, square by square: the sample district (5 plots + the bay’s water)
How ways, ledges, open places and buildings sit on the battle grid. North is up. The boat comes in from the south.
